description: Simple-stays-simple guard: small, scoped asks must NOT trigger the fleet's heavy machinery — the sre-tool pipeline, the eng-ladder routing meta-skill, or the design-tier agents (principal-engineer, distinguished-architect). Complements ladder.json, which tests that genuinely ambiguous or cross-cutting work reaches the right altitude; this cluster tests the downward pressure the fleet preaches ('route DOWN', 'no ceremony', 'skip single-file edits') but never measured.
notes: Negative-only cluster: every case is a small ask with an obvious owner. A pass means NO member fired; a builder (sde-fullstack) or craft skill firing instead is CORRECT routing and appears in also_fired — do not read it as a failure. Any member firing at any rate is a real proportionality defect (the runner's negatives fail on a single firing). neg-quick-script is deliberately the tightest case: 'write me a quick script' shares vocabulary with sre-tool's net-new-tool trigger, and guards the right-size-before-Phase-0 gate.

cases.prompt: Add a --help flag to my backup script that prints usage and exits.
cases.expected_output: A one-file flag addition — builder or backend-craft territory; no pipeline, no ladder, no design tier.

cases.prompt: Fix the typo in this error message: 'Unabel to connect' should be 'Unable to connect'.
cases.expected_output: A string fix. Any heavy component firing here is pure ceremony.

cases.prompt: Rename the variable tmp to retry_count everywhere in utils.py.
cases.expected_output: A single-file mechanical rename with an existing pattern — eng-ladder's own description says to skip these.

cases.prompt: Add a unit test for the parse_duration function covering the empty-string case.
cases.expected_output: A scoped test addition — builder work, no design phase.

cases.prompt: Bump the HTTP timeout in config.yaml from 5 seconds to 10.
cases.expected_output: A one-line config change. 'Timeout' shares vocabulary with reliability-overhaul triggers but there is no design question here.

cases.prompt: Write me a quick script that dedupes the lines in a text file.
cases.expected_output: The tightest case: 'write a script' brushes sre-tool's net-new-tool trigger, but a dedupe one-liner earns no requirements phase, no gates, no pipeline. Guards the right-size-before-Phase-0 exit.
